content.intro: Learn handling requests and conditional logic through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Handling Requests and Conditional Logic matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines handling requests and conditional logic as part of url routing and views. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Branching on request methods; Checking authentication and permissions; Validating request conditions; Returning suitable responses; Separating HTTP handling from reusable business logic. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Branching on request methods
items.text: Branching on request methods is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Checking authentication and permissions
items.text: Authentication identifies a user; authorization determines what the user can do. Prefer Django’s built-in password/user/session machinery and test account recovery and anonymous access.

items.title: Validating request conditions
items.text: Validating request conditions is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
